subject: BrightLeaf — sudden 429s and latency spikes (rate window fence failure)
messages:
From: Chris Miller <chris.miller@brightleaf.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: P1: Burst of 429s + latency spikes impacting BrightLeaf production

Rafael —

We just started seeing a big surge of 429s and end-to-end latency spikes across our integration (region: us-east-1) beginning ~07:58 UTC. Our customers are reporting timeouts in the UI and our ingestion pipeline is backing up. Sample error rates attached (brightleaf_429s_sample_0812.txt).

Key details:
- First observed: 2028-06-14T07:58:13Z
- 429s and 503s with elevated p95/p99 latency (p99 jumped from ~350ms to >3s)
- We are on Redwood model v1.3 pinned in our route (no recent changes on our side)

Can someone from Redwood confirm whether any new rate/guardrail changes rolled out? This is customer-impacting; please escalate. We need an ETA to restore normal throughput.

Thanks,
Chris
Director, Site Reliability
BrightLeaf Health

---
Attachment: brightleaf_429s_sample_0812.txt (text file, 42KB)

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Miller <chris.miller@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: P1: Burst of 429s + latency spikes impacting BrightLeaf production

Thanks for flagging, Chris — and sorry for the disruption. Looping in engineering and account.

Neha / Laura / Connor: BrightLeaf is seeing a sudden spike of 429/503 with high tail latency in us-east-1. They report no config changes on their side; their route is pinned to v1.3. Can we get an immediate triage? Hypothesis from initial telemetry: a new guardrail rollout (burst safety fence) may be firing too aggressively for sustained burst patterns and dropping requests by classifying them as abusive.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether any burst/fence policy changes were deployed to us-east-1 around 07:30–08:30 UTC?
- If a policy rollout is the culprit, can we rollback the policy or open a regional exception to restore capacity?
- Short-term mitigation: increase BrightLeaf's quota window and lift the safety fence for their tenant while we investigate.

I've shared the customer's sample logs. Marissa, can you keep BrightLeaf on the line for updates and patch in CS for credits/communication?

I'll coordinate exec updates if this becomes prolonged.

— Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0127

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Miller <chris.miller@brightleaf.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: P1: Burst of 429s + latency spikes impacting BrightLeaf production

Quick triage summary from infra (observed at ~07:55 UTC):
- We rolled out "burst_fence_v2" to us-east-1 at 07:40 UTC as part of a gradual policy rollout intended to clamp abusive sustained bursts.
- The new fence uses a rolling window heuristic that mis-classifies the client's steady elevated traffic pattern (long-lived ingestion streams) as an attack surface; it triggers an aggressive request-shed path that returns 429s and routes some traffic into the backpressure safety path causing higher latency.
- This matches BrightLeaf's error pattern and timestamps.

Immediate actions I am executing now:
1) Emergency rollback of burst_fence_v2 on us-east-1 (started 09:03 UTC) — fallback to previous fence_v1 parameters.
2) Open a tenant-level exception (temporary) to increase BrightLeaf quota window to 2x for the next 30 minutes.
3) Telemetry: enabling high-resolution traces for the tenant to capture KV-cache and batching behavior for the postmortem.

Runbook referenced: Confluence /runbooks/fence-policy-rollback (attaching a trimmed runbook).

Attachment: runbook-fence-rollback.md (markdown, 12KB)

ETA: rollback should complete in ~10–12 minutes and we will closely monitor for rejections and p99. If we do not see recovery within 20 minutes we will escalate to a hotfix of the kernel-level gating logic.

— Laura
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Miller <chris.miller@brightleaf.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: P1: Burst of 429s + latency spikes impacting BrightLeaf production

Rollback update:
- rollback started at 09:03 UTC and completed at 09:14 UTC for us-east-1.
- We've opened tenant exception and bumped BrightLeaf quota window by 2x at 09:08 UTC.
- Initial telemetry: 429 rate dropped by ~92% within 3 minutes post-rollback; p99 latency decreased from >3s down to ~480ms over the next 7 minutes.

Monitoring: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/tenant/brightleaf/latency (live)

Next steps:
- Keep the exception for 30 minutes while we replay traces collected during the event.
- We will schedule a canary of fence_v2 with the corrected rolling-window parameters in a sandbox tenant first.
- Postmortem owner: Neha is taking the lead; Connor + Laura will provide kernel and policy diffs.

Attachment: rollback-notes-20280614.txt (text, 3KB)

— Connor
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Chris Miller <chris.miller@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: P1: Burst of 429s + latency spikes impacting BrightLeaf production

Thanks team — great fast action. Neha here (Support/CS lead) — I will own the customer communication and postmortem coordination.

Immediate customer-facing steps:
- Marissa, please confirm the compensation/credits offer. I recommend offering BrightLeaf a two-week service credit and a postmortem within 72 hours.
- I'll coordinate the meeting with their SREs for a deep-dive and to review the corrected fence parameters.

Internal asks for postmortem:
- Full diffs between fence_v2 and fence_v1 (policy rules + rolling window config)
- Kernel gating metrics and KV-cache pressure traces for the affected window (07:45–09:15 UTC)
- Who approved the v2 rollout and what the canary scope was?

I'll draft the exec brief once we have the telemetry and postmortem timeline.

— Neha
Head of Support & Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

We accept the two-week credit and look forward to the postmortem. Please share the meeting invite and the corrected fence parameters so our engineering team can validate.

Best,
Chris
